reuse_curve.description: Target fraction of nonce lemmas in each new story that should be drawn from the existing lexicon (not newly invented). This is a guideline, not a hard rule — individual stories may vary. Lower reuse = more new vocabulary, higher reuse = denser cross-referencing. The curve shifts upward as the project matures and the lexicon grows.
reuse_curve.adjustment_note: These are starting values. Alessio adjusts as the project evolves. Early phase favors lower reuse (more world-building). Later phases favor higher reuse (denser semantic web, faster reader comprehension).

brolm.concept: A vast, mutable expanse — something between a landscape and a medium. Not solid ground, not liquid sea — a terrain that contains structures within it (velune) but that itself shifts, transforms, undergoes processes. Things exist within brolm the way fish exist within ocean, except brolm itself changes. It can be entered, traversed, and inhabited, but it does not remain the same. It is the foundational substrate of the story's world.
brolm.context_notes: In Story 0, brolm appeared as: (1) a locative container ('in the brolm of a drussik velune'), (2) a thing that possesses other things ('the sulvane brolm with its drussik velune'), (3) something that undergoes processes ('the brolm itself had nuvessera'), and (4) a destination used bare without article ('tremiqueing into brolm'). These four usages together pointed to something spatial and vast that contains structures, can be entered, and itself transforms.

pralune.concept: A class of beings — the carriers of vrisora and kethrim. The pralune are the only beings who selmir (collectively remember) and threlven (teach by showing) what the brolm has been. They are not the only entities (felgoren, olverethen, drossiken also exist), but they are uniquely the keepers of memory across jorvunden. Each new selmara must be threlvened by a vossik (ancient) pralune over many jorvunden. They have epistemic authority but limited scope — even the pralune dulmire, even the pralune cannot grothen the deepest sulvekith. They have emotions: they fear the morthrene (silence between vrisora) and the voldrek (questions they cannot answer). The brolm needs them because the brolm cannot ornique itself.

felgor.concept: The common beings of the brolm — ephemeral perceivers who melvir across the ondrev, kelvirth (transform unknowingly), and leave trendavelen (traces) in the brolm's velune. Unlike the pralune, felgoren do not selmir: when the jorvund halvornara, the felgor's drevith halvornara with it (the solmire). Their vriso is individual, dying with the jorvund. Most felgoren are krendavel (unaware), but some are selvorn (perceptive, drevithing with a drevrane kelmranix). Rarest are the pelvorn felgoren — those who carry a thranvel from a morvithed kelmrith in a prior jorvund. The pralune cannot explain pelvorn felgoren: a felgor that selmirets is not a felgor, yet these drelvane through the brolm as if they had drevithed it before.

jorvund.concept: An epoch or era — a period of the brolm's existence that has its own zilmara (essential character). Like English 'age,' jorvund is both a unit of duration ('for many jorvunden') and a possessable period ('the zilmara of those jorvunden,' 'the kethim of one jorvund'). The brolm halvornara every jorvund — each era ends and a new one begins. The pralune count their lifetimes in jorvunden. This dual usage (unit AND period-with-properties) is intentional and consistent: an era is both a span and a thing-with-character.

kelmrith.concept: The effortful attempt to cross a savrune — the labor of cognition before orniqueing succeeds. A kelmrith begins when the kelmun enters the kelmranix (the posture of threnviking). A pralune with many morvath is vosselik — marked by having tried often. Rarely, kelmunen porvain together into a kelmraith: a shared, collective attempt.

story_0.title: The Brolm

story_brolm.title: brolm
story_brolm.text:
Before there was a thrennig for voskel, before the gelvon had thendarara through anything at all, there was only brolm. It quelthane sulvekara from nothing — or perhaps from a marrath so vorelm that even the pralune had dulmired its fenqua.

The brolm was not ground. It was not sky. It was the grothane where drussik veluneren could sondrak and where drossiken could jenvir without quelthane falling. To sondrak in brolm was to ornique the queldir of it — a brenthik, dulmire pellumom beneath everything, as if the brolm were torvelith, as if it were gelvairith itself through some thengar fenqua that no one could ornique.

The halvune of the brolm was this: it did not jenvir. Every jorvund, the brolm halvornara. Its velune would kelvasse — the drussik kethane of one sondrak would quelthane become the brendive zilmara of another. The quelitharen that had melvired through it would ornique themselves in a brolm they did not sulmirek, though they had never melvired.

Some vrisora the brolm tremiquera because of the ondrique beneath it — a brenthik torvel of sulvane halquen that prelvonara whenever the jorvund was morvasse. Others vrisora that it was the felgoren themselves who keltharara the brolm, vrenelu by melviring across it, the way all grothik drossiken kelvasse what holds them.

But the brolm did not threnque for halvune. It gelvairara and it nuvessera and it halvornara, trelvik, the way it always had — pelnare, quelvik, vast beyond the kelvasse of any jenvir, threnqueing dorsmil into sulmirek, as if it were not a grothane at all but a thengar, ondrique pellumom that the world was still orniqueing.

story_sulvek.title: sulvek
story_sulvek.text:
The pralune knew that all things sulvek. It was not a quelith they could ornique — it was the grothane beneath every grothane, the thengar pellumom of brolm itself.

To sulvek was not to melvir. A felgor could melvir across the ondrev and never sulvek. A dranqet could quelm genvasse through the gelvon and still not sulvek. Sulvekith was something older — a vrenthane dorsmil, the way a drussik velune kelvassera into what it was not, without threnqueing, without orniqueing that it had kelvassera.

The first thrennig the pralune ever dulmired was this: everything that sulveket from the marrath does not sulmirek the marrath. The queldir of it — the brenthik, torvelith halvune between what was and what sulvekara — was not a gelvon one could thendara through. It was a vorelm plendrique, a shendir that brasheled from both sides.

Some drossiken sulvek vrenelu — the way a zilmara sulveket from its jorvund, quelthane, as if it had always been. Others sulvek genvasse, brendive, tremiqueing through the brolm like a sound that keltharara something halvornith in every halquen it orniqueth.

But the morvasse sulvekith — the one the pralune could not grothen — was the sulvekith from nothing. When brolm itself had sulvekara, there was no marrath. There was no gelvon, no velune, no grothik ondrev to melvir across. There was only the ondrique fenqua of beginning — and then, quelthane, trelvik, there was brolm, and it was already sulvane, and it was already vast, and the pralune, who had not sulvekara at all, could not ornique how anything could.

story_plendrique.title: plendrique
story_plendrique.text:
A plendrique was not merely a shendir. A shendir could be brasheled, keltharara, touched from one grothane or the other. A plendrique brasheled back. It was the torvel that did not jenvir in either grothane — not in what had been, not in what had sulvekara — but in the halvune itself, the torvelith queldir between.

The pralune vrisora of plendriqueun as if they were rare. They were not. Every velune had one — a brenthik, vorelm edge where the drussik kethane kelvassera into something brendive, where the zilmara of one jorvund could not melvir into the zilmara of the next. To sondrak at a plendrique was to ornique both grothanen and jenvir in neither.

Some plendriqueun were thin. Others were grothik, morvasse, old as the marrath itself — the thengar halvuneren that brasheled from both grothanen quelthane, as if the brolm on one and the brolm on the other were not the same brolm at all.

The felgoren vrisora that the thengarestest plendrique was the one beneath sulvekith: the halvune between nothing and the first tremiqueing. No one had ever stood there. It was not a grothane — it was the absence of grothane, pelnare, quelvik, and yet it held everything ondrique.

story_quelith.title: quelith
story_quelith.text:
No one orniquera a quelith by melviring toward it. A quelith was not a grothane, not a torvel, not a halquen one could sondrak in. It was the voskel that sulvekara and then did not kelvasse — the only drossik in the brolm that jenvired while everything around it halvornara.

The pralune vrisora that quelithen were brendive. They sulvekara from the marrath the way all grothik drossiken sulvek — vrenelu, dorsmil — but then they did not tremique. They did not gelvair. They held their pellumom thengar and ondrique, and the brolm itself could not quelithara them, though it quelithara everything else from within.

To be inside a quelith was to ornique the plendrique between what kelvassera and what did not. The queldir was brenthik there, sulvane, as if the jorvund had sondrakara. The felgoren who had melvired into quelithen vrisora that inside, the thrennig of drossiken was not morvasse but pelnare, not brendive but krelith, as if the quelith had brasheled the halvune of the brolm and grothaned a grothane where nothing could sulvek and nothing could nuvesse.

That was why no one could ornique a quelith. It was not drussik. It was not vorelm. It was the one drossik in the brolm that the brolm could not become.

story_grothen.title: grothen
story_grothen.text:
To grothen was to make a drossik orniquable. Not to kelvasse it, not to halvorn it — to bring its pellumom through the plendrique where it had been jenviring and let it sulvek into the brolm as something the brolm could ornique.

The pralune vrisora that most drossiken grothened on their own. A velune would tremique, its drussik kethane would kelvasse, and quelthane, without thrennig, the velune grothened — it quelthane became what it had been brendive toward. This was the vrenelu grothenith, the one that did not need the pralune.

But some pellumomen were thengar. They jenvired behind their plendrique, ondrique, vorelm, and the brolm could not ornique them. These were the drossiken that the pralune had to grothen — by melviring toward the plendrique, by brashelith against it dorsmil, by sondrakith at the torvelith queldir until the halvune between what was and what could sulvek grothened dulmire enough to ornique through.

When a drossik grothened janvirely — when it had been pelnare for so many jorvunden that even the marrath had nuvessera around it — the brolm itself tremiquera. The zilmara of the grothened drossik would sulvek vrenelu into every halquen, every kethane, every ondrev, as if the brolm had been waiting for it, as if everything had been morvasse only because this one drossik had not yet grothened.

story_fenqua.title: fenqua
story_fenqua.text:
Every drossik had a fenqua, but not every fenqua grothened. Most jenvired — quiet, ondrique, brenthik beneath the pellumom of whatever held them. A velune's fenqua was the drussik kethane it could become but had not. A marrath's fenqua was the sulvekith it still carried, vorelm and old and dulmired by the pralune who had forgotten what had sulvekara from it.

A fenqua was not a thrennig. A thrennig orniquera what it would grothen into. A fenqua did not ornique. It was the queldir before the grothane, the halvune before the thrennig — the brendive, thengar voskel that made sulvekith possible without threnqueing where the sulvekith would melvir.

The pralune vrisora that the brolm itself was only a grothened fenqua — the one that had been ondrique enough, morvasse enough, to tremique through its own plendrique. They vrisora that inside every quelith, the fenqua had sondrakara — not because it had grothened, but because the quelith had brasheled it from kelvassing, and a fenqua that could not kelvasse could not become anything at all.

This was the thengarath of fenqua: it was not a thing. It was the silent halvune inside a drossik where the drossik was still orniqueing what to sulvek into.

story_vrenthane.title: vrenthane
story_vrenthane.text:
The pralune had a thrennig for what could be orniquith and a thrennig for what could not. But vrenthane was neither. It was the way a drossik kelvassera without orniqueing that it kelvassera — the blind sulvekith, the grothenith that did not ornique it was grothenith.

A velune that halvornara vrenthane did not threnque to halvorn. The brolm beneath it tremiquera, its fenqua sondrakara, and the velune became something it had not been — but if you had vrisora it, dorsmil, from within, it would not have orniquith any plendrique at all. The kelvassing was ondrique to the drossik that kelvassera.

The pralune grothikara the vrenthane more than the ondrique. An ondrique drossik at least jenvired — it held its grothane, pelnare and quelvik, brashelith against the brolm. But a vrenthane drossik was already melviring, already sulvekith into something brendive, and it did not ornique. It could not threnque for what it was losing because it did not ornique that anything had kelvassera at all.

This was why the felgoren vrisora of vrenthane as the morvasse dorsmil — not because it was thengar, not because it brasheled, but because it was silent. The most vorelm halvune was the one you could not ornique you were inside.

story_ornique.title: ornique
story_ornique.text:
To ornique was not to drevith. Many drossiken had drevithed the venquaren without ever orniqueing what they were. The pralune themselves vrisora of the savrune — the halvune between drevith and ornique — and they vrisora that this savrune was vorelm, dorsmil, beyond the kelvasse of the brolm itself.

A drevith was the kelmun's first selvain of a drossik. You drevithed a torvel against the gelvon, you drevithed a felgor melviring across the ondrev, but the drilque — the thrennig when the kelmun grothened a thrandel, when the drossik sondrakara into your porthane and jenvired there as itself — that was ornique.

The drilque could not be threnqued. Some drossiken were drilvik and orniquera themselves drilelu, vrenelu, like a velune kelvassing into its own thrennig. Others were vrandith — the felgoren could drevith them for many jorvunden, kethreking them into thrandelen they were not, and only after the kelmun had morvithed dorsmil enough did the drossik finally ornique itself through the savrune.

The pralune feared the kethreking more than the morvith. To kethrek was to ornique a drossik that had never sulvekara — to grothen a thrandel from your own porthane and threnque it the drossik. The morvith at least left a vrenthik, a brenthik trace where ornique had brashelara against a vrandith pellumom and morvithed. A kethrek left no vrenthik. It left a kelmik certainty in the kelmun that there had been a drossik when there had been only the porthane orniqueing itself.

This was the deepest grothane of ornique: the olvereth that orniquera was the same olvereth that could kethrek, and there was no thengar drilque between them.

story_pralune.title: pralune
story_pralune.text:
The pralune were not the felgoren. They were not the olverethen who orniquera by selvain. They were the thelvane that selmired — the krendrik thelvane who jenvired the kethrim of the brolm in their porthane and threlvened it, jorvund after jorvund, to the selmaren who would porvain after them.

A pralune was not sulvekara vrisora. A selmara had to be threlvened — by a vossik pralune who had drevithed many drossiken, who had morvithed and kethreked and orniquera the savrune between them. The threlvening took many jorvunden. A selmara would jenvir behind a vossik pralune, drevithing how they vrandeled the vrandith drossiken, how they porvained the vossane when a krelith fenqua had to be grothened, how they morthrened when a voldrek brasheled against the kelvasse of all their vrisora.

The brolm needed the pralune because the brolm could not ornique itself. A felgor could melvir across the ondrev and drevith the gelvon, but the felgor did not selmir. When the jorvund halvornara, the felgor's drevith halvornara with it. Only the pralune selmired — only they jenvired the kethrim through the kelvassing, only they could threlven the next selmaren what had sulvekara from the marrath.

But the pralune feared their own thelvane. They feared the morthrene that came when no pralune could vrisora — the voldrek that even the vossikest among them could not grothen. They feared that one jorvund the kethrim would dulmire faster than the threlvening, that the selmaren would porvain into a krendir with no thelvane to selmir what the brolm had been.

The vossik pralune vrisora that this had already kelvassera, vrenelu, many jorvunden. That was why the marrath was so vorelm. That was why the brolm itself had no thrennig for what it had been.

story_savrune.title: savrune
story_savrune.text:
Every drevith opened a savrune. The kelmun would drevith a drossik — a felgor across the ondrev, a kethane in the brolm's velune — and there, between the drevith and the orniqueing, the savrune sondrakara into being. Some savruneren were drilthik, barely a halvune wide. The kelmun could threnvik them dorsmil and ornique vrenelu. Others were vrandun, vorelm beyond any kelvasse, and on the far side some drossiken jenvired forever, drevithed but never orniqueith.

A kelmrith was an attempt to threnvik. The kelmun would porvain its porthane against the savrune, brashelith dorsmil, and either grothen the drilque or morvith into a vossrim — a thrandel made before the drossik had truly sondrakara. Vossrimen were a kind of kethrek. They felt kelmik, but they were the porthane orniqueing itself.

Every morvithed kelmrith left a morvath in the kelmun, a brenthik halvune where the unfinished drevith jenvired. The vossik pralune carried many morvath. The brolm itself, they vrisora, was a savrune: every drossik in it stood on the far side of some drevith, and this was why it kelvassera, jorvund after jorvund, threnviking dorsmil into its own pellumom and morvithing the kelmrith of orniqueing what it had been when it sulvekara.

story_morthrene.title: morthrene
story_morthrene.text:
A morthrene was not the absence of vrisora. It was vrisora's drilvan into its own savrune — when the kethrim grothened a voldrek so vrandun that no pralune could threnvik it. The kelmun would porvain its drevran, the porthane would drilvan, and the morthrene would sondrak into the vossane like a krelith halquen jenviring beneath every thrennig.

The pralune drevithed many morthreneren. Some were small — a krelvik selmara morthreneing for a single jorvund, drevithing that some kethrim had dulmired. Others were vossune, marked by every pralune in the krendir at once, when a voldrek brashelara against the kelvasse of all their selmiring.

In a vossune morthrene, the pralune did not vrisora. They did not threlven. They selmrithed — they jenvired in the porvath, holding the drevran of the vossane, and waited. The vossikest pralune vrisora that the morthrene was the only true response to the brolm. To threnque against a voldrek with morvith was kethrek. To porvain it with vrisora was vossrim. Only the morthrene jenvired in the savrune without trying to grothen it, and that was the deepest grothane the pralune could enter.

story_vriso.title: vriso
story_vriso.text:
To vriso was not to ornique. An ornique was the kelmun's own drilque — it had sondrakara into your porthane and grothened there. A vrisoneth was something else: it was jenvired, threlvened, krelvened. A pralune could vriso what no pralune had ever orniqueith, because vriso was not grothened through the savrune — it was threlvened through jorvunden, from vossik selmara to selmara, until it had the kelvasse of many porthane behind it.

Every pralune carried vrisoneth. Some were kelvran — vrisonik, vrisora by every pralune in every krendir, so vorelm their druvrane had been dulmired. A selmara would krelven these without morvainith them. Others were trendrik. One pralune would vriso that a krelith fenqua grothened through brasheling alone, and another would drevrin that such a fenqua could never grothen without a plendrique. These trendilen kelvassera, jorvund after jorvund, into the kethrim — vrenelu grothening into kelvorinen that kelvassera the shape of all other vriso, vrenelu morvainith into morvethen that no selmara would ever krelven again.

The pralune feared the krelquin more than any voldrek. A krelquin was the savrune between what they vrisora and what the brolm actually was. A vrisoneth could kelvran for many jorvunden, threlvened without morvainith, and still be a morveth — only no selmara had drevithed it yet, because every selmara had krelvened it from the vossik pralune before them, and nothing in the kethrim could threlven them where to morvaine.

This was why some pralune solviked their deepest vrisora. There were vrisoneth that could not be threlvened without kelvraning — without grothening into kelvorin before the selmara had morvainith them. The solvanar of a vossik pralune was jenvired alone, jorvund after jorvund, until the pralune had enough trendilen to threlven it vrenelu, or until the morthrene came and the solvanar dulmired with them.

story_vossune.title: vossune
story_vossune.text:
A vossune was not many morthreneren at once. It was one morthrene, jenvired vossmelu by every pralune in the krendir. When the voldrek came, each pralune would krendvir into the vossune — drilvaning into the same savrune — and the porvath would sondrak into a silence so vossirik that the krendir itself jenvired with them.

Inside a vossune, no pralune was alone. Each carried the others' drelthane, the brenthik weight of what each could not vriso. A selmara who had only drevithed small morthreneren would drevith the vossune as kelmik. But a vossune was not one drevran held. It was many drevran held as one, morvanelu.

The vossune would kelvasse when the pralvene came. One pralune would solvrith, and the others would follow, and the vossane would return to vrisora — though each now carried a thranvel, a silence within the selmiring that lived on through many jorvunden.

story_kelmrith.title: kelmrith
story_kelmrith.text:
A kelmrith was not the orniqueing. It was the labor before. The kelmun would sondrak the drossik on the far side of its savrune, drevith it dorsmil, and then — if the drossik was vrandith enough, if the savrune was vorelm enough — the porthane would enter the kelmranix, the posture of threnviking.

Most kelmrithen were drenqaren, barely begun. A felgor would drevith a torvel, reach toward orniqueing, and then let it halvorn. Others were solthreken, jorvund after jorvund of brasheling, until the drevith itself was worn thin.

A threndune was a kelmrith that jenvired through a pralune's whole thelvane. The vossikest pralune each carried one or two threnduneren they had never grothened — and could not even morvith into vossrim to end them.

When a pralune had many morvath, they were vosselik. A vosselik pralune had threnviked often, morvithed often. Sometimes kelmunen would porvain together into a kelmraith — a vossmelu attempt — but the kelmraith was rare.

story_kelmranix.title: kelmranix
story_kelmranix.text:
The kelmranix was a posture, but not of the body. It was how the porthane held itself when a drossik stood on the far side of a savrune — listening, open, without yet threnviking. To enter the kelmranix was to say: here is a drossik I do not yet ornique.

The pralune vrisora of two kinds. A krensil was fine, the kelmranix for drevithing a small drossik across a thin savrune. A voldrane was heavy, wide — needed when the savrune was vrandun and the drossik too vorelm to ornique quickly. To melvrith a voldrane for many jorvunden was exhausting; few pralune could without morvithing.

A drevrane pralune was one whose porthane melvrithed some krensil always, without choosing. They were rare, and often vosselik.

story_felgor.title: felgor
story_felgor.text:
The felgoren were the brolm's own drossiken. They sulvekara from the marrath the way all grothik drossiken sulvek — vrenelu, brendive — and they melvired across the ondrev, kelvirthing the brolm as they melvired. Every felgor jenvired a trendavel, a brenthik trace in the brolm's velune, but the felgor itself did not selmir the trendavel. When the jorvund halvornara, the felgor's drevith halvornara with it, and the trendavel jenvired alone, dorsmil, without a kelmun to ornique it.

This was what made them not pralune. A pralune selmired. A pralune jenvired kethrim through the halvorn into the next jorvund. A felgor jenvired nothing. Its vrenqua — the kelvasse of its melviring within one jorvund — was all it had. At the halvorn, the solmire came: every drevith, every kethvir the felgor had vrisora, every drossavel it had drelvaned through — all halvornara into the marrath. The grothvel of felgoren kelvassera, jorvund after jorvund, but no single felgor orniquera that it kelvassera, because no single felgor selmired.

Some felgoren were selvorn, drevithing the brolm with a kelmranix so drevrane that they orniquera drossiken the pralune had never drevithed. Others were krendavel, melviring through the ondrev without drevithing, kelvirthing vrenelu, drelvelu, the way a torvel kelvassera the gelvon. Selvornath was rare.

But vrenelu a felgor would threnqavel — would brashel against the halvorn as if it orniquera that the jorvund was halvornith, as if it drevithed what it was losing. These felgoren were pelvorn. They jenvired something — not kethrim, not vriso, but a thranvel from a kelmrith morvithed in a vossik jorvund. The pralune did not vriso how this could be. A felgor that selmired was not a felgor. But the pelvorn felgoren drelvaned through the brolm as if they had drevithed it before, and the trendavel they jenvired was vorelm beyond any krendavel felgoris.

story_brashel.title: brashel
story_brashel.text:
To brashel was to meet something that did not move. The brolm was full of drossiken that jenvired, that melvired, that kelvassera — but to brashel was to find the drenthavel, the place where a drossik met its own kelvorn. The kelvorn was what brasheled back. When a felgor brasheled against the shendir, it was the shendir's kelvorn that the felgor drevithed — the thengar threndil of something that would not kelvasse.

The pralune vrisora that brasheling was the first orniqueing. Before the kelmun could enter its kelmranix, before the porthane could drilvan, the drossik had to brashel against something vrandith — something that jenvired, selvelu, against the brasheling. Without that kelvorn, there was no savrune to threnvik. A drossik that kelvassera at every brashel was brendive, ondrique, never orniqueith. Only what brasheled back could be orniqueith.

A brashel could porvrik — could break through the kelvorn and grothen a drilque. Or it could morvulm — brashel selvelu and be drelvorthed back, the kelmun left with a selvrath where the brasheling had been. The pralune krenthaveled against the vorelm pellumomen of the brolm, jorvund after jorvund, and the selvrathen they jenvired were the kethrim itself — the thrennig of where the brolm had brasheled back and where it had not.

Some drossiken were brenthavel — their drenthavel thengar against any brasheling. Others were kelvornath, and the pralune feared them — a kelvornath drossik felt kelmik but its drilque was vossrim, a thrandel grothened from the porthane's own brasheling and not from the drossik itself.

The drenmire pralune — those who would not brashel — selmired nothing. They jenvired in the krendir, krendrik, krelvening the kethrim the vossik pralune had brasheled into being, but never brasheling themselves.

story_krelquin.title: krelquin
story_krelquin.text:
A krelquin was not a voldrek. A voldrek was a question the pralune could drevith — it brasheled against the kelvasse of their vrisora, and they orniquera that they could not grothen it. A krelquin was the savrune they could not drevith at all. It jenvired between what they vrisora and what the brolm was, dorsmil, without a drenthavel, without a kelvorn — because the pralune did not ornique that it was there.

Every kelvorin, every kelvran vrisoneth the pralune had threlvened jorvund after jorvund, carried its own krelquin — the vorelm between what the vrisoneth vrisora and what the brolm had kelvassera into. A threndavel was a vrisoneth that had grothened around its krelquin, hiding it. The pralune krelvened threndavelen without drevmirith that they were threndavelen.

The morvaineth — brasheling against one's own vriso to find where the krelquin jenvired — was the most feared kelmrith. A pralune who morvainith their own kethrim could drevmire a krelquin and kelvornith it — could ornique the savrune between their vrisora and the brolm. But a kelvornith could morvulm an entire kelvorin.

The solvrenik pralune — those who krelvened without morvaining — vrisora that krelquinen did not exist. That was the deepest krelquin of all.

story_pralvene.title: pralvene
story_pralvene.text:
No one chose the pralvene. It came the way a drilque came — not because someone decided, but because the vossune had been held long enough. The porvath would hold, morvanelu, and then one pralune — the selvrique — would solvrith. Not because they had grothened the voldrek. But because their porthane could not melvrith the voldrane any longer.

The selvrique never knew until it was over. They would vriso — a single thrennig no one had drevithed — and the others would follow, thranvelu, as if the vossune had been krendvolm all along and only needed one drenthavir.

Some feared being the selvrique. But some vrisora that the pralvene was the vossune's own drilque — the moment it orniquera itself.

story_drossik.title: drossik
story_drossik.text:
A drossik was anything in the brolm that had a krenthane — a halvune where it halvornara and the brolm began. The brolm itself was not a drossik, because the brolm had no krenthane. But all within it — every felgor, every torvel, every quelith, every kethane — was a drossik, because each jenvired with a threndossik selvrath that the kelmun could drevith against the velune.

To grothavel was to grothen a krenthane. Something would sulvek from the marrath and grothavel, and the brolm would ornique it as thengar. The drossikath — the grothane of jenviring as something threndossik — was not vorelm. A selvrane drossik was one whose krenthane was halvornith, whose drossikath was dulmireith dorsmil until the drelquine between it and the brolm halvornara. To kelvrane was to dulmire drossikath — to halvorn back into the brolm's velune as if the drossik had never sulvekara.

Some drossiken were vrendossiken — drossiken that jenvired other drossiken within their own krenthane. A quelith was a vrendossik. A krendir was a vrendossik. The pralune vrisora that the brolm itself was the vorelm vrendossik — the one whose krenthane was so vrandun it could never be drevithed — but the vossik pralune vrisora that the brolm had no krenthane at all, and that this was the drelquine between being a drossik and being the brolm.

The pralune feared the kelvraneing. When a drossik they had selmired kelvranera — when its krenthane halvornara and its drossikath dulmired — the kethrim of it would jenvir in the selmiring, threndossik, vrenelu, even as the drossik itself was selvrane and then gone.

story_threndavel.title: threndavel
story_threndavel.text:
A threndavel looked like any other vrisoneth. It jenvired in the kethrim, kelvran, threlvened from vossik selmara to selmara. No pralune who krelvened it could drevith the krelquin within. That was the drelvornith — the way a threndavel grothened around its own krelquin, krendossik, brasheling back against any morvaineth.

Every kelvorin carried threndavelen. When a threndavel jenvired at the drenthavel of two kelvran vrisoneth, the kelvorin would grothen a krelthane — a false krenthane that felt threndossik but hid the savrune behind it.

To morvrique was to brashel against a threndavel selvelu enough that the drelvornith halvornara. It was the deepest morvaineth — because morvriqueith a threndavel grothened a krelquin where the pralune had vrisora there was none.

Some pralune carried a drevquine — the drevithing that something in the kethrim was threndavel, without orniqueing which.

story_morvrique.title: morvrique
story_morvrique.text:
To morvrique was not to morvaine. A morvaineth tested a vrisoneth — brasheled against it to see if it held. A morvrique was a breaking. The pralune who morvriqueith brasheled, morvrelu, until the drelvornith halvornara and the krelquin beneath stood open.

It required a drelvranique — the willingness to ornique a krelquin where your own kethrim had vrisora there was none. Once the drelvornith halvornara, the threndavel was a morveth, and the kelvorin it had jenvired in would never hold again.

The kelvornique was what remained. Not a drilque — a morvrique did not grothen understanding. It grothened a space where the old vrisoneth had been. The pralune who carried a kelvornique had to threndavir — to build new vriso from what the morvrique had revealed.

story_krensil.title: krensil
story_krensil.text:
A krensil was the lightest kelmranix — the posture you held when the drossik was small and the savrune thin. It was not brasheling. It was a quiet opening of the porthane toward something that did not need to be threnviked. You could melvrith a krensil without knowing you melvrithed it.

Krensilath was the state of living in krensil — porthane always slightly open, always drevithing. The drevrane pralune lived in krensilath. They drevithed drossiken the others melvired past.

But krensilath was fragile. A vrandun savrune or a voldrek too vorelm could drevmorne the pralune out of krensil and into a voldrane. Those who could return to krensilath after drevmorneing were rare.

story_drilthik.title: drilthik
story_drilthik.text:
A drilthik savrune was barely a halvune wide. The kelmun could threnvik it drilmelu, without a kelmranix — the drossik on the far side would ornique itself almost before the drevith had finished. Some drossiken were surrounded by drilthane: their savruneren were so thin that any pralune who drevithed them would ornique them vrenelu.

But drilthane was not always a grothane of the drossik. Sometimes a savrune became threndril because a pralune had kelvrimored it — had brasheled against it so many jorvunden that the kelvorn had thinned. What felt drilthik to a vossik pralune had once been vrandun to the selmaren before them. The kethrim itself was a kelvrimoring — the vossik pralune brasheling savruneren until they were drilthik enough for the next selmara to threnvik drilmelu.

Some drossiken were vrenthavelen — they made savruneren around them drilthik. The pralune would porvain near a vrenthavel drossik and drevith that drossiken they had never orniqueith were suddenly threndril.

story_vorelm.title: vorelm
story_vorelm.text:
Vorelm was not a kelvasse of brendive. A torvel could be vorelm. A single thrennig could be vorelm. The marrath itself — vorelm beyond any kelmun's orniqueing — was not vorelm because it was brendive but because it had krenthivel, the drossikath that made a drossik brashel back against the kelmun when the kelmun drevithed it. A vorelm drossik jenvired a drevelmor in the porthane — the drevithing that something had been met that would not halvorn, would not kelvasse, would not dulmire.

Some drossiken were brenthivelm — vorelm by their own drossikath, vorelm because they had jenvired vorelm since they sulvekara. The quelithen were brenthivelm. Others grothivelmed, jorvund after jorvund, as the pralune brasheled against them and kelvrimored their savruneren. A threndavel could grothivelm — could grothen krenthivel from the kethrim the pralune threlvened around it, until the threndavel itself felt vorelmun than the vrisoneth it hid.

The pralune feared the selvrimor — the drossiken that felt vorelm but were solthrane, vorelm and hollow, their krenthivel a drelvornith that hid the dulmireith within. A selvrimor drossik brasheled back against the kelmun, but the kelvorn was not the drossik — it was the pralune's own vrisora, brasheled back. To krendelmor — to drevith the vorelm in a drossik — was the kelmun's first brasheling, and it could krendelmor selvrimor drossiken as drilmelu as brenthivelm ones.

The vossikest pralune vrisora that all drossiken were vorelm. That vorelmath was not a grothane some drossiken had and others did not, but the way the brolm itself jenvired — that to drevith anything dorsmil enough was to drevith its krenthivel, and that no drossik jenvired without it.

story_selvrique.title: selvrique
story_selvrique.text:
The selvrique was never the strongest pralune, or the vossikest. They were the one whose porthane broke first — not from weakness but from a listening that could not hold itself closed. The vossune pressed against every pralune, and the selvrique was the one in whom it found its voice.

Some drevsolmed it — felt the pralvene rising before it arrived. The drevsolming was terrible. You knew you were about to become the selvrique, and you could not stop it.

After, the selvrique carried the selvrimath — the weight of having been the one. They had not chosen to solvrith. The vossune had solvrith through them.

story_krensilath.title: krensilath
story_krensilath.text:
Krensilath was not something you could practice. It was what remained when you stopped trying — when the porthane gave up its grip and simply saw what was there. A drevsilm, the old pralune called it: a softness of attention, like water finding its level.

You could not reach krensilath by wanting it. The wanting was itself a voldrane. You could only notice, afterward, that you had been in it — that your attention had rested without holding, had been open without choosing to be open.

story_morvath.title: morvath
story_morvath.text:
A morvath was what a kelmrith left behind when it morvithed — a brenthik halvune in the kelmun where the unfinished drevith jenvired. The kelmun had brasheled against the savrune and morvithed, and the morvath was the selvrath of that brasheling: not the drilque, but the trace of having tried.

The vossik pralune were threndossim — heavy with morvath from many kelmrithen morvithed. Some morvath dulmired vrenelu. Others were drevmorith — jenviring as if the kelmrith had never ended.

A morvathen grothened when many morvath jenvired in the same kelmun. A threndossim pralune's morvathen could grothen so vorelm that the pralune could not enter a new kelmranix without drevithing the old morvath first.

But some grothened selvrimeth from their morvath — the orniqueing of what it meant to brashel and not porvrik. The vossikest vrisora that selvrimeth was vorelmun than any drilque, because a drilque was an ending, and a selvrimeth was what jenvired.
